ican: I can calculate the input speed of a gear train.
I can calculate the number of teeth on a gear.
I can explain why a compound gear train is used.
I can describe how to change the direction of the output.

cloze.title: Say it the exam way
cloze.text:
Working backwards uses the [[same|opposite]] relationship. Put in what you know, then [[rearrange|guess]] for the unknown.

Gears on the same shaft turn at the same [[speed|size]]. A number of teeth is a [[whole number|decimal]] with no unit.

A compound gear train gives a large reduction in speed using [[smaller|larger]] gears, so it fits in a small [[space|motor]].

Each mesh [[reverses|keeps]] the direction. To change the direction of the output, add an [[idler|extra compound]] gear between two meshing gears.

check.q: A 20-tooth driver gear meshes with a 60-tooth driven gear. The driven gear turns at 50 revs min⁻¹. Calculate the input speed.
check.a: input speed × 20 = 50 × 60, so input speed = 3000 ÷ 20 = 150 revs min⁻¹

check.q: A 15-tooth driver gear turns at 400 revs min⁻¹. The driven gear must turn at 100 revs min⁻¹. Calculate the number of teeth on the driven gear.
Explain why a compound gear train is used instead of a simple gear train.
check.a: It uses smaller gears (cause), so it fits inside a small space (effect).

check.q: A gear train has three meshes. State if the output turns the same way as the input, or the opposite way.
check.a: The opposite way (an odd number of meshes).

check.q: Describe how to change the direction of the output without changing its speed.
check.a: Add an idler gear between two meshing gears.

check.q: A 12-tooth driver gear meshes with a 36-tooth gear that turns at 40 revs min⁻¹. Calculate the input speed.
check.a: input speed × 12 = 40 × 36, so input speed = 1440 ÷ 12 = 120 revs min⁻¹

paper2.alt: A photograph of a wind farm. A pupil's model of the wind turbine's compound gear train: the turbine blades turn a 48-tooth gear, which meshes with a 12-tooth gear. A 56-tooth gear on the same shaft meshes with an 8-tooth gear on the generator, which turns at 308 revs per minute. (c) Describe an advantage of using a compound gear train over a simple gear train. 1 mark.

mi.alt: Marking instructions for 2015 Question 10(c). Compact size with a large speed change possible. 1 mark.

paper2.alt: 3D printers allow individual users to quickly manufacture complex products from a computer model. Part of the gear mechanism in the 3D printer: the motor at 1500 revs per minute turns a 16-tooth gear, which meshes with a 48-tooth gear. A 12-tooth gear on the same shaft meshes with gear D, whose output speed is 150 revs per minute. (d) Calculate the size of gear D. Show all working. 4 marks.

mi.alt: Marking instructions for 2016 Question 11(d). Input speed x input size = output speed x output size: 1500 x 16 = output speed x 48, so output speed = 500 revs per minute, 2 marks. Then 500 x 12 = 150 x D, so D = 40 teeth, 2 marks. Or: velocity ratio = 1500 / 150 = 10 : 1; 10 = 48/16 x D/12; D = 40.

paper2.alt: (c) The mechanical system in a self-balancing scooter: the motor at 4800 revs per minute turns gear A with 10 teeth, which meshes with gear B with 30 teeth. Gear C with 12 teeth on the same shaft meshes with gear D on the wheel, which turns at 200 revs per minute. Calculate the number of teeth on gear D. 4 marks. (d) Explain how this mechanical system could be made more efficient. 2 marks.

mi.alt: Marking instructions for 2017 Question 12. (c) 4800 x 10 = output speed x 30, so output speed = 1600 revs per minute. 1600 x 12 = 200 x size of D, so D = 96 teeth. Or: velocity ratio = 4800 / 200 = 24 : 1; 24 = 30/10 x D/12; D = 96. (d) Lubrication, bearings or a slippier material (cause, 1 mark) to reduce friction or energy loss to heat and sound (effect, 1 mark).

paper2.lead: Build It D4 in your booklet (the scooter drive) is based on this question. Parts (a) and (b) are logic.

paper2.alt: A snow making machine in a container, and a free body diagram of the forces on its base (from parts (a) and (b)). Ice is broken up by a cutter driven by a compound gear train: the motor at 1980 revs per minute turns gear A with 12 teeth, which meshes with gear B with 108 teeth. Gear C with 16 teeth on the same shaft meshes with gear D on the cutter, which turns at 55 revs per minute. (d) Calculate the number of teeth on gear D. 4 marks. (e) Describe a modification to the compound gear train that results in gear D rotating in the opposite direction to gear A. 2 marks.

mi.alt: Marking instructions for 2021 Question 14. (d) 1980 x 12 = output speed x 108, so output speed = 220 revs per minute. 220 x 16 = 55 x gear D, so gear D = 64 teeth. Or: velocity ratio = 1980 / 55 = 36 : 1; 36 = 108/12 x D/16; D = 64. (e) Insert an idler gear between gears A and B, or between C and D: 1 mark for using an additional gear, 1 mark for its position.

paper2.alt: A photograph of a road gritter, and its low-temperature warning circuit (from earlier parts). The gear train that drives the salt spreader: the motor turns gear A with 12 teeth, which meshes with gear B with 120 teeth. Gear C with 16 teeth on the same shaft meshes with gear D with 96 teeth on the spreader, which turns at 12 revs per minute. (e) Calculate the input speed of the motor. 4 marks.

mi.alt: Marking instructions for 2022 Question 10(e). 12 x 96 = output speed x 16, so the speed of gears B and C = 72 revs per minute. 12 x input speed = 72 x 120, so input speed = 720 revs per minute (2 significant figures). 1 mark each for substitution and answer, twice. Do not accept RPM. A gear ratio method also gets full marks.

paper2.alt: A combine harvester with its reel and cutter bar. Part of its drive mechanism: the input at 3750 revs per minute turns gear A with 10 teeth, which meshes with gear B with 50 teeth. Gear C with 12 teeth on the same shaft meshes with gear D on the output, which turns at 250 revs per minute. (c) Calculate the number of teeth on gear D. 4 marks.

mi.alt: Marking instructions for 2023 Question 13(c). 3750 x 10 = output speed x 50, so output speed = 750 revs per minute. 750 x 12 = 250 x gear D, so gear D = 36 teeth. Or: velocity ratio = 3750 / 250 = 15 : 1; 15 = 50/10 x D/12; D = 36.

paper2.alt: A photograph of a laminator, and its temperature indicator circuit (from earlier parts). A large reduction in speed is required for a feed roller to slowly move the plastic sleeve and paper through the laminator. (f) Explain why a compound gear train is more suitable than a simple gear train to create this large reduction in speed in the laminator. 2 marks.

mi.alt: Marking instructions for 2023 Question 14(f). A compound gear train uses smaller gears (cause, 1 mark), which makes it able to fit inside the small space of the laminator (effect, 1 mark). Do not accept high velocity ratio as a cause or effect.

paper2.alt: A photograph of an electric bike at a charging point. The motor and gear train: the motor turns gear A with 16 teeth, which meshes with gear B with 48 teeth. Gear C with 16 teeth on the same shaft meshes with gear D with 64 teeth on the output, which turns at 120 revs per minute. (a) Calculate the rotational speed of the motor. 4 marks.

mi.alt: Marking instructions for 2024 Question 9(a). 120 x 64 = input speed x 16, so input speed = 480 revs per minute. 480 x 48 = input speed x 16, so input speed = 1440, written 1400 revs per minute (2 significant figures). 1 mark each for substitution and answer, twice. Do not accept RPM. A gear ratio method also gets full marks.

paper2.alt: A battery powered delivery robot with cameras, sensors, motorised wheels and a storage compartment. Its drive mechanism, drawn from the side: the motor at 1920 revs per minute turns gear A with 8 teeth, which meshes with gear B with 32 teeth. Gear C on the same shaft meshes with gear D with 64 teeth on the wheel, which turns at 120 revs per minute. (c) State the name of this drive mechanism. 1 mark. (d) Calculate the number of teeth on gear C. 4 marks.

mi.alt: Marking instructions for 2026 Question 8. (c) Compound gear (train). (d) 1920 x 8 = output speed x 32, so the speed of gears B and C = 480 revs per minute. 480 x size of C = 120 x 64, so C = 16 teeth. Or: velocity ratio = 1920 / 120 = 16 : 1; 16 = 32/8 x 64/C; C = 16.

errors: Start from the data booklet relationship and work one pair at a time. In 2024, pupils who used the gear ratio did less well (2024 course report).
Explain why compound: smaller gears (cause), so it fits in a small space (effect). "A high velocity ratio" got no mark (2023).
Say where the idler goes: between gears A and B, or between C and D. One mark is for the extra gear, one for its place (2021).
Write the unit as revs min⁻¹. "RPM" got no mark (2022, 2024).
The marking gives 1440 as 1400 revs min⁻¹, to 2 significant figures (2024).
